tips_en: Start with Paper 1 (ABSeeker) — it offers a clean methodological contribution (Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment) with strong empirical wins on BrowseComp (55.3% with context management), making it the most immediately actionable read for anyone working on agent training. Paper 2 (ToolArtist) is a natural follow-up since both papers tackle RL-based training of agentic systems, but Paper 1's credit-assignment insight is more generalizable. Paper 3 (MirageBench) is worth reading afterward as a sobering counterpoint: while Papers 1 and 2 push agentic capabilities forward, Paper 3 reveals that even strong personalized LLMs fabricate user attributes 41.6% of the time, and — strikingly — models' own self-assessments negatively correlate with actual over-inference (the Self-Monitoring Inversion, ρ=−0.60), a finding that should temper enthusiasm about deploying these increasingly capable agents without robust external oversight.
tips_zh: 建议先读论文1（ABSeeker）——它提出了清晰的回溯式信用分配方法（ABC），在BrowseComp上取得了强劲结果（启用上下文管理后达55.3%），对从事智能体训练研究的读者最为实用。论文2（ToolArtist）是自然的后续阅读，因为两篇都聚焦于基于强化学习的智能体系统训练，但论文1的信用分配洞见更具普适性。论文3（MirageBench）值得放在最后作为反思：在论文1和论文2不断推进智能体能力的同时，论文3揭示了个性化大语言模型平均41.6%的用户属性是无中生有的，且模型的自评与实际过度推断呈负相关（自监控反转，ρ=−0.60），这一发现提醒我们在部署日益强大的智能体时必须配备可靠的外部监督机制。
